editorial.calculatorIntro: This calculator is set to CERSW18000-H. Capacity Only estimates a full spool; Backing + Main Line estimates backing beneath the working length you choose. Both are estimates. The listed retrieve is available for the handle-turn estimate.
editorial.setupIntro: Start with the line range that suits your rod and fishing. You can fill with main line or use backing beneath a shorter working length. For braid, secure the base against slipping and spool under steady tension; stop at a sensible clearance below the lip.

editorial.capacityIntro: Daiwa lists J-Braid capacities for this 2026 model, but no factory mono capacity. The table keeps that distinction. Other lines can fill differently, even at the same pound-test rating, so use the calculator as a starting estimate and check the spool as you wind.

editorial.specsIntro: These are the published 2026 US CERSW18000-H specifications, not those of the older Certate SW. Retrieve falls as line leaves the spool, and maximum drag is an upper rating, not a suggested fishing setting.
editorial.faqBraid: 80-100 lb braid is the practical ReelCalc range for this reel. For offshore fishing, balance the working line and reserve you need against the strength required by your rod, rig, and target fish. The lighter end leaves more line in reserve; the stronger end suits heavier rigs when the rest of the tackle is matched to them. Choose the leader separately for the fish and structure.
editorial.faqCapacity: Daiwa lists J-Braid at 65 lb / 460 yards and 80 lb / 330 yards. No mono capacity is published in the cited 2026 U.S. table. The calculator can estimate other lines from the available reference, but that is not a factory mono rating.
